source.original_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel sigma algebra; zero dimension is allowed. Let alpha,beta>=0, eta be real, V:E->R. Assume exactly alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. All conclusions hold for every y,r in E, initial phase z0=(x0,p0), integer n>=0 and finite T>=0.
Set c=y-eta*grad V(r). For z=(x,p), define Phi_u(z)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p). Define h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p-[2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2]h_r(x)) with real division totalized by 0/0=0, lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta)max(0,<p,h_r(x)>), and Lambda_z(u)=integral from0 to u of lambda_r(Phi_s(z)) ds for u>=0, using Lebesgue measure.
A tagged record is either live(a,z), with a>=0, or stopped; Hist_n is the type of all n+1 records. Let Delta_n(T) be the strict simplex 0<t1<...<tn<T. Write a0=0, ai=ti (1<=i<=n), a_(n+1)=T. Given t in Delta_n(T), define z_i=S_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1))) for1<=i<=n and K_n(t)_j=live(a_j,z_j). The literal Lean nonnegative conversions preserve these nonnegative times. Define qReal_n(t)=product_(i=1)^n [lambda_r(Phi_(a_i-a_(i-1))(z_(i-1))) exp(-Lambda_(z_(i-1))(a_i-a_(i-1)))], q_n=ofReal(qReal_n).
For arbitrary histories let readTime(live(a,z))=a and readTime(stopped)=0; d_n(T,h)=max(T-readTime(h_n),0). Put W(live(a,z),u)=ofReal(exp(-Lambda_z(u))) and W(stopped,u)=0. Define rho_n(T,t)=q_n(t) W(K_n(t)_n,d_n(T,K_n(t))). Here ofReal(x) is max(x,0) embedded into extended nonnegative reals; no probability law or normalization is assumed in this deterministic identity.
Define Path_T as all phase-valued functions on[0,T]. The total interpolation Psi_n(h)(s) starts at z0 and scans records j=0,...,n in order: a live(a,z) record with a<=s replaces the accumulator by Phi_(max(s-a,0))(z); otherwise it is unchanged. Set Gamma_n(t)=Psi_n(K_n(t)). Extend this particular prescribed path to all real times by gamma(s)=Gamma_n(t)(min(max(s,0),T)). This extension agrees with Gamma on[0,T]; no topology on an entire function space is asserted.
Define R(x,p)=(x,-p), U_y(x,p)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta)+||p||^2/2 and w_y(z)=exp(-U_y(z)). Let ell=(Lebesgue measure on E) times (Lebesgue measure on E), and m_n,T be the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n by the inclusion of the strict simplex Prefix_n(T). Equip X_n,T=(E times E) times Prefix_n(T) with its Borel product/subtype sigma algebra and phase-first measure mu_n,T=ell times m_n,T, without normalization or a factorial factor.
For every n>=0 and T>=0 there exists one map rho:Prefix_n(T)->Prefix_n(T), with (rho(t))_i=T-t_(n+1-i) in one-based coordinates, which serves all y,r and observables below. For q=(z,t) set A(q)=Gamma_(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T), Theta(q)=(R(A(q)),rho(t)), and W(q)=ofReal(w_y(z))*rho_(y,r,z,n,T)(t); the density rho remains the actual q_n times terminal survival defined above. For every measurable F:X_n,T->[0,infinity],
integral W(q)*F(Theta(q)) dmu_n,T(q) = integral W(q)*F(q) dmu_n,T(q).
Both integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals and may be infinite, with 0*infinity=0. Measurability of F is the test-domain condition; the actual weight's joint measurability, map's measure preservation and weight matching are proved internally from the six analytic assumptions. No finite-mass, finite-integral, normalization or positivity-of-rate premise is added. The result includes n=0, T=0, rank-zero E, zero normals and zero rates; the simplex is empty for n>0,T=0. This extends the source bounded nonnegative test substitution to measurable ENNReal tests without asserting integrability. It proves only the unnormalized finite-sector change of variables. Normalized Gibbs averaging, countable summation, signed-test integrability, invariance, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, simulation errors, expected costs and full paper/composition results remain separate.

    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let rate : E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun xRef z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Λ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℝ := fun y xRef z t =>
      ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), rate xRef (Φ y xRef s z)
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
    let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let qReal : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ∏ i : Fin n,
        rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)
          (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)) *
        Real.exp (-Λ y xRef (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)
          (Real.toNNReal (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)))
    let q : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (qReal y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let liveTime : Rec → ℝ≥0 := fun r => r.elim Prod.fst (fun _ => 0)
    let d : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Hist n → ℝ≥0 :=
      fun n T h => T - liveTime (h ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩)
    let weight : E → E → Rec → ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0∞ :=
      fun y xRef r u => r.elim
        (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-Λ y xRef a.2 u))) (fun _ => 0)
    let Path : ℝ≥0 → Type _ := fun T => {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T} → E × E
    let Ψ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Hist n → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T h s =>
        Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z j => (h j).elim
          (fun a => if a.1 ≤ s.val then Φ y xRef ((s.val - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2 else z)
          (fun _ => z)) z₀
    let Γ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => Ψ y xRef z₀ n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let ρ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => q y xRef z₀ n T t *
        weight y xRef ((K y xRef z₀ n T t) ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩)
          (d n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t))
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let U : E → E × E → ℝ := fun y z =>
      V z.1 + ‖z.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η) + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2
    let w : E → E × E → ℝ := fun y z => Real.exp (-U y z)
    let ell : Measure (E × E) := (volume : Measure E).prod (volume : Measure E)
    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0, ∃ rho : Prefix n T → Prefix n T,
      (∀ t : Prefix n T, ∀ i : Fin n, (rho t).val i = (T : ℝ) - t.val i.rev) ∧
      ∀ y r : E,
        let A : (E × E) × Prefix n T → E × E :=
          fun q => Γ y r q.1 n T q.2 ⟨T, le_rfl⟩
        let Theta : (E × E) × Prefix n T → (E × E) × Prefix n T :=
          fun q => (R (A q), rho q.2)
        let W : (E × E) × Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ :=
          fun q => ENNReal.ofReal (w y q.1) * ρ y r q.1 n T q.2
        ∀ F : (E × E) × Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable F →
          (∫⁻ q, W q * F (Theta q) ∂(ell.prod (m n T))) =
            ∫⁻ q, W q * F q ∂(ell.prod (m n T))
decoder_context: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including rank zero; real Hilbert gradient and Frechet derivative.
Fin n is zero-based; Fin.rev sends i to n-1-i; Fin.cons prepends and Fin.induction recursively constructs a finite sequence; Fin.foldl visits ascending indices.
Real division by zero is zero; Real.toNNReal is positive part; nonnegative subtraction is truncated; Sum.inl is a live record and Unit is cemetery.

The real path extension is clamped to the closed nonnegative horizon; interval integrals use real Lebesgue measure. ENNReal.ofReal maps a real to its positive part in extended nonnegative reals. Literal let definitions are definitions, not supplied hypotheses.

    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) : actual_weighted_sector_statement hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη := by
  classical
  unfold actual_weighted_sector_statement
  intro c Φ S rate Λ Rec Hist Δ Prefix zAt K qReal q liveTime d weight Path Ψ Γ ρ R U w ell m n T
  obtain ⟨rho, hrho, h97⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualEndpointTimeReversal.actual_endpoint_time_reversal_laws
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T
  obtain ⟨rho101, hrho101, h101⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualPrescribedWeightedDensity.actual_prescribed_weighted_density_balance
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T
  have halign : rho101 = rho := by
    funext t
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext i
    exact (hrho101 t i).trans (hrho t i).symm
  subst rho101
  refine ⟨rho, hrho, ?_⟩
  intro y r A Theta W F hF
  have hTheta : MeasurePreserving Theta (ell.prod (m n T)) (ell.prod (m n T)) :=
    h97.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2 y r
  have hbalance (q : (E × E) × Prefix n T) : W q = W (Theta q) :=
    (h101 y r q.1 q.2).2
  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualFiniteCountPath.actual_finite_count_path_law
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hρjoint : Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
      ρ p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) := (hZ.2.2.2.2 n T).2.2.1
  have hemb : Measurable (fun q : (E × E) × Prefix n T => (((y, r), q.1), q.2)) :=
    ((measurable_const.prodMk measurable_fst).prodMk measurable_snd)
  have hρ := hρjoint.comp hemb
  have hU : Continuous (U y) := by
    exact ((hV.continuous.comp continuous_fst).add
      (((continuous_fst.sub continuous_const).norm.pow 2).div_const (2 * η))).add
      ((continuous_snd.norm.pow 2).div_const 2)
  have hw : Continuous (w y) := Real.continuous_exp.comp hU.neg
  have hW : Measurable W :=
    (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp (hw.measurable.comp measurable_fst)).mul hρ
  calc
    (∫⁻ q, W q * F (Theta q) ∂(ell.prod (m n T))) =
        ∫⁻ q, W (Theta q) * F (Theta q) ∂(ell.prod (m n T)) := by
      apply lintegral_congr
      intro q
      rw [hbalance q]
    _ = ∫⁻ q, W q * F q ∂(ell.prod (m n T)) := hTheta.lintegral_comp (hW.mul hF)

#print axioms actual_weighted_sector_lintegral
end

reconstruction.text:
Anonymous theorem reconstruction

Ambient data and hypotheses.
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive group structure and Borel measurable structure. Dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E -> R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable. Let alpha,beta be nonnegative real numbers, regarded also as ordinary real scalars, with alpha>0 and alpha<=beta. For every x,v in E, assume
  alpha ||v||^2 <= D(DV)(x)[v][v] <= beta ||v||^2.
Let eta be a real number with eta>0 and beta eta<=1. The gradient below is the real Hilbert-space gradient of V. All following displayed constructions are definitions from these data, not additional assumptions or freely supplied interfaces.

Deterministic phase-space constructions.
For y,r in E, put c=y-eta grad V(r). For z=(x,v) in E x E and a real time u define
  Phi(y,r,u,(x,v)) = (c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)v,
                      -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)v).
Set g_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r) and define
  S_r(x,v) = (x, v-[2 <v,g_r(x)> / ||g_r(x)||^2] g_r(x)),
  rate_r(x,v) = sqrt(eta) max(0,<v,g_r(x)>).
Real division by zero is zero. Thus S_r(x,v)=(x,v) when g_r(x)=0; there is no requirement that this gradient difference be nonzero. For h>=0 define the real cumulative rate
  Lambda(y,r,z,h) = integral from 0 to h of rate_r(Phi(y,r,u,z)) du,
where the integral is the real interval integral with respect to real Lebesgue measure.

Finite ordered times and event states.
For an integer n>=0 and a finite nonnegative real horizon T, let D(n,T) be the subset of R^n consisting of t=(t_1,...,t_n) with
  0<t_1<...<t_n<T.
The Lean definition expresses this by strict monotonicity after prepending zero and by the upper bound for every coordinate. For n=0 all conditions are vacuous, so D(0,T) is a singleton, including T=0. Prefix(n,T) is the subtype of R^n specified by D(n,T). Set t_0=0. Given an initial phase state z_0 and t in Prefix(n,T), recursively define, for j=1,...,n,
  delta_j=t_j-t_(j-1),
  b_j=Phi(y,r,delta_j,z_(j-1)),
  z_j=S_r(b_j).
Here b_j is the state immediately before the prescribed event and z_j is the state after its reflection. The delta_j are strictly positive. zAt is the sequence z_0,...,z_n. K is the history with n+1 live records (t_j,z_j), j=0,...,n. In the literal definition times are converted by Real.toNNReal, which takes positive part and hence leaves these valid nonnegative times unchanged.

Histories, path evaluation, and terminal survival.
The full record type Rec is the disjoint union of ([0,infinity) x (E x E)) and a one-point cemetery. Hist(n) is the set of arrays of n+1 such records. liveTime is the stored nonnegative time on a live record and zero on the cemetery. d(n,T,h) is the truncated nonnegative difference T-liveTime(h_n). For a duration u>=0, weight(y,r,record,u) is exp(-Lambda(y,r,z,u)), embedded into the extended nonnegative reals, for a live record whose stored phase state is z; for the cemetery it is zero. Its stored time does not otherwise enter weight.

Path(T) is the space of all functions from the closed nonnegative interval [0,T] into E x E. For a general history h, Psi(y,r,z_0,n,T,h)(s) is computed by starting from z_0 and visiting records in ascending index order j=0,...,n. A live record (a,z) with a<=s replaces the current value by Phi(y,r,s-a,z); a live record with a>s or a cemetery record leaves it unchanged. The subtraction used here is nonnegative truncated subtraction, equal to ordinary subtraction when a<=s. Consequently it is the last eligible record by index, not necessarily the largest record time for an arbitrary unsorted history, that determines the final value. Gamma(y,r,z_0,n,T,t) is Psi evaluated on the particular ordered, fully live history K. Equivalently, on this valid history Gamma(s)=Phi(y,r,s-t_j,z_j), where j is the largest index with t_j<=s. This includes the after-reflection state at an event time, and includes both endpoints 0 and T. In particular its terminal value is Phi(y,r,T-t_n,z_n), with t_n=0 and z_n=z_0 when n=0. The actual theorem only evaluates this path at T; it does not quantify over path-space tests or assert a path-space identity. The packet's contextual convention about a clamped real-time extension adds no such extension or claim to this displayed statement.

Prefix and complete finite-history densities.
For each valid prefix define the nonnegative real number
  qReal(y,r,z_0,n,T,t)
    = product over j=1,...,n of
        [rate_r(b_j) exp(-Lambda(y,r,z_(j-1),delta_j))].
q is qReal embedded in the extended nonnegative reals by ENNReal.ofReal. Empty products equal one. Define
  density(y,r,z_0,n,T,t)
    = q(y,r,z_0,n,T,t)
      * exp(-Lambda(y,r,z_n,T-t_n)),
with the exponential embedded in the extended nonnegative reals. This is exactly the literal rho/density definition using K, d and weight; the live ordered histories make its final duration T-t_n. The terminal survival factor remains present for n=0. Every potential event factor uses the rate at the state b_j before reflection, not at z_j. These definitions use real exponentials and extended-nonnegative multiplication; they contain no normalization constant.

Energy and integration measures.
Define R(x,v)=(x,-v),
  U_y(x,v)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta)+||v||^2/2,
  w_y(x,v)=exp(-U_y(x,v)).
Let ell be the product of Lebesgue volume on the position E and Lebesgue volume on the velocity E, in that order. Let m(n,T) be Measure.comap of Lebesgue volume on Fin(n)->R along the inclusion of Prefix(n,T) into that finite-coordinate real vector space. In ordinary terms this is the induced Lebesgue measure on the ordered open simplex of event times, with no n! factor or probability normalization. For n=0 it is the mass-one measure on the sole empty time vector. The final integration measure is ell.prod(m(n,T)): the phase-state variable (position,velocity) is the first product component, and the ordered time vector is the second. If written as iterated nonnegative integrals, this has outer phase-state integration and inner prefix-time integration.

Exact quantified assertion.
For every integer n>=0 and every finite T>=0, there exists a map revTimes:Prefix(n,T)->Prefix(n,T) such that, in one-based coordinates,
  revTimes(t)_j = T-t_(n+1-j),  j=1,...,n.
Equivalently the original zero-based coordinate i is sent to T-t_(n-1-i). The map is chosen after n,T and before y,r, so the same map works for every y,r in E. Its coordinate formula specifies its value completely.

For every y,r in E, on Q=(E x E) x Prefix(n,T), write a point as p=(z_0,t) and define
  A(p)=Gamma(y,r,z_0,n,T,t)(T),
  Theta(p)=(R(A(p)),revTimes(t)),
  W(p)=ENNReal.ofReal(w_y(z_0)) * density(y,r,z_0,n,T,t).
Then for every measurable F:Q->[0,infinity],
  integral_Q W(p) F(Theta(p)) d(ell.prod(m(n,T)))(p)
    = integral_Q W(p) F(p) d(ell.prod(m(n,T)))(p).
These are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals with values in the extended nonnegative reals, not real integrals. Thus the assertion includes cases where either side is infinite; it asserts equality of the extended values and requires neither integrability nor boundedness nor finiteness of F. Standard extended-nonnegative conventions apply, including 0 times infinity equals 0.

Scope and degenerate cases.
There is no probability normalization, sum over event counts, random event-count variable, stationary-process construction, non-explosion assertion, path-space reversal assertion, or complexity assertion in this theorem. It establishes the displayed weighted integral identity separately for each fixed n and T. It does not separately state measurability, bijectivity, an involution law, or ordinary unweighted measure preservation of Theta; those must not be substituted for its literal conclusion. revTimes has the stated coordinate property, but the conclusion is precisely its existence together with the integral identity.

When n=0, Prefix is a singleton, K contains just (0,z_0), q=1, the density is exp(-Lambda(y,r,z_0,T)), and A=Phi(y,r,T,z_0). When T=0 and n>0, the strict simplex is empty and both integrals are zero; revTimes is the unique empty map. When T=0 and n=0, the sole path value is z_0, the density is one, and Theta flips the initial velocity. Dimension zero is permitted; in that case all rates vanish, all positive-count densities vanish, and no positive-dimensional assumption may be inserted. A zero event rate at any prescribed event likewise makes its full density zero. All horizons, coordinates, energies, and parameters are finite real or nonnegative-real objects; only F, density/weights as typed, and integral values inhabit extended nonnegative reals. The constructed weights are pointwise finite, though this assertion does not supply a finiteness conclusion for all the displayed integrals. All parameters alpha,beta,eta,V,E are shared throughout, and no extra constants or uniform estimates are asserted.
